channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyz Citizen Awarded Order of Friendship by Russian President Putin
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin presented the Order of Friendship to a Kyrgyz citizen, Zukhra Shidakova. Meanwhile, Kyrgyzstan's Interior Minister spoke at an international conference in Astana on combating cybercrime, noting an increase in AI-related fraud threats. A fire occurred at an ethno-complex in Alamedin district, destroying part of a kitchen and a yurt. Former traffic police chief Talantbek Isaev was fined for illegal parking in Tokmok. The resort town of Cholpon-A is undergoing reconstruction, with its mayor discussing its past and future development. President Sapar Japarov instructed the cabinet to consider banning energy drink production and imports within a month. Kyrgyz participants were recognized as best media specialists at the International Space Games.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Deputy Chairman: Key Rate May Decrease Below 10% in Three Years
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank Deputy Chairman, Nodirbek Ochilov, stated that the key rate may be gradually reduced below 10% within the next three years. This process will primarily depend on inflation falling to the target level. Further details are available through the provided link.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Cultural Heritage Initiative Approved by UNESCO Executive Board
item.description: The UNESCO Executive Board has unanimously approved Uzbekistan's initiative to preserve cultural heritage, with an international symposium to be held in Khiva. Pakistani agency "Associated Press of Pakistan" reported on Uzbekistan's international initiatives, including social reforms, technological diplomacy, and investment projects. Discussions also covered a phone call between the foreign ministers of Uzbekistan and Pakistan and cooperation in regional academic matters. The "Kazinform" agency highlighted consultations between the security councils of Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan on combating cybercrime, terrorism, AI threats, and managing transboundary water resources.

item.title: Presidents of Uzbekistan and Tajikistan Arrive in Astana for Aqaba Process Summit
item.description: The Presidents of Uzbekistan and Tajikistan have arrived in Astana to participate in the Aqaba Process Summit. Tajik President Emomali Rahmon was welcomed by Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev also arrived for the summit, which aims to strengthen international cooperation in combating terrorism, extremism, and transnational crime. Earlier, President Tokayev met with Jordan's King Abdullah II, and both leaders exchanged state awards.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Expand Critical Mineral Production and New Projects
item.description: Uzbekistan is focusing on expanding its mining sector, with plans for new projects and increased production of critical minerals. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed development strategies for "Navoiyuran" and the "Uzbek Metallurgical Plant." The country aims to leverage its mineral resources to boost value-added production and exports, responding to a global surge in demand for critical minerals.

item.title: 19 European Flights Received Bomb Threat Messages in 24 Hours
item.description: Nineteen flights across Europe received bomb threat messages within a 24-hour period, according to The Guardian. Flights between 14 countries, including France, Spain, and the UK, were affected. While all landed aircraft were cleared, the EU is investigating potential coordinated actions and monitoring the situation closely.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Police shoot tires of fleeing vehicle driven by minor
item.description: In Almaty region, police fired at the tires of a fleeing vehicle driven by an underage driver without a license. The minor endangered road users and attempted to evade authorities. The driver was apprehended, and his father faces administrative responsibility for neglecting parental duties. Investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Hydropower Capacity Grows to 2.5 GW with 106 Plants
item.description: Uzbekistan has expanded its hydropower capacity to 2.5 GW, operating 106 hydropower plants (HPPs), up from 36 previously. In January-September, electricity generation reached 6,642.7 kWh, exceeding the plan by 120%. The company aims to improve investment attractiveness through cost optimization and digital transformation.

item.title: Uzbekistan discusses steps towards World Trade Organization membership
item.description: Uzbekistan held a meeting with the Chair of the Working Group on Uzbekistan's accession to the WTO and the Director of the WTO's Accessions Division. Discussions covered the accession process, economic and legislative reforms, and cooperation between Uzbekistan and South Korea. Training for international trade specialists was also addressed.

item.title: Shymkent blogger known as 'Askо' sentenced to 4.5 years for extortion
item.description: A blogger from Shymkent, known online as 'Askо', and two accomplices have been sentenced to 4.5 years in prison for extorting businessmen and officials. The group filmed videos potentially damaging to reputations and demanded money to suppress them.

item.title: Former MP urges EU to recognize Taliban's gender apartheid and designate them terrorists
item.description: Former Afghan MP Baktash Siawash addressed the European Parliament, urging the EU to formally recognize the Taliban's "gender apartheid" in Afghanistan. He called for an end to normalizing relations with the Taliban and requested they be designated a terrorist organization, criticizing European governments' diplomatic engagement with the group.

item.title: Latvia and Lithuania Consider Deploying Nuclear Weapons Amid Russian Threats
item.description: Latvia and Lithuania are exploring options to strengthen their security in light of Russia's nuclear threats. While initial political steps have been taken, deploying nuclear weapons requires agreement with allies and significant domestic preparations. The possibility of such deployment is being discussed.

item.title: Kassym-Jomart Tokayev Welcomes Emomali Rahmon on Official Visit to Astana
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon arrived in Kazakhstan for an official visit, where he was welcomed at Astana airport by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. The visit, scheduled from November 5-7, will focus on strengthening strategic partnership and discussing cooperation in trade, economy, and other sectors.

item.title: Turkmenistan President Arrives in Astana for Akaba Process Summit
item.description: The President of Turkmenistan, Serdar Berdymukhamedov, has arrived in Astana to participate in the Akaba Process summit. This initiative focuses on coordinating security efforts and combating terrorism. The summit aims to foster cooperation among participating nations.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Welcomes Tajik President Rahmon in Astana
item.description: President Emomali Rahmon of Tajikistan has arrived in Kazakhstan for an official visit, welcomed by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev at the Astana airport. The leaders are set to discuss strengthening strategic partnership and alliance relations.

item.title: Juvenile Crime in Kazakhstan Decreases by 6.9 Percent
item.description: In the first nine months of 2026, juvenile offenses in Kazakhstan dropped by 6.9%. Positive trends were observed in several regions, including Pavlodar and East Kazakhstan. New courses on law and order are being introduced in schools.

item.title: Tajikistan President Arrives in Astana for Central Asia Security Summit
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon arrived in Astana for an official visit and to participate in the Aqaba Process summit. He was met at the capital's airport by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. The summit will focus on artificial intelligence security, countering its use for terrorism, and strengthening international cooperation on technological challenges.

item.title: Interpol Fugitive from Kazakhstan Arrested in Thailand for Large-Scale Fraud
item.description: A 24-year-old Kazakhstani citizen, wanted by Interpol for fraud and money laundering totaling over 560 million tenge, has been arrested in Thailand. He was apprehended in a Phuket guesthouse. Authorities suspect he created over 20 fake companies with accomplices to launder money and evade taxes. He also overstayed his visa.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Establish Integrated Agro-Food Park with EDB Support
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will establish an integrated agro-food park following a trilateral agreement signed at the Regional Industrial Development Forum. The Eurasian Development Bank will provide $370,509 in financing, with participation from UNIDO. The project aims to develop agricultural processing and attract investments.

item.title: UN: Afghanistan Imports Over 80% of Electricity, Faces Energy Deficit
item.description: The UN Development Programme reports Afghanistan imports over 80% of its electricity, costing more than $280 million annually. Despite solar potential, most regions lack reliable power. Addressing this requires joint efforts, as no single institution can solve the issue alone.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Fruit and Vegetable Exports Exceed 1.56 Million Tons, Valued at $1.3 Billion
item.description: Uzbekistan's fruit and vegetable exports reached over 1.56 million tons in the first nine months, valued at $1.3 billion. Vegetables accounted for the largest share. The country emphasizes product quality, storage, packaging, and logistics to meet international standards and maintain competitiveness.

item.title: Kazakhstan President and King of Jordan Exchange State Orders During Official Visit
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and King Abdullah II of Jordan exchanged state orders during the King's official visit. Tokayev awarded the Al-Farabi order, while Abdullah II presented the highest Jordanian award. The exchange highlighted the deepening strategic partnership between the two nations.

item.title: International Conference in Astana Discusses Global Transformations and Central Asia's Regional Cooperation
item.description: An international conference, 'Think Road Forum 2026,' is being held at the University of World Economy and Diplomacy in Astana, focusing on global transformations and regional dynamics in Central Asia. Discussions cover geopolitical competition, economic ties with China, transport corridors, and regional security.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's State Banks Halt Operations with 284 Companies Due to Sanction Risks
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's state banks have ceased business relations with 284 companies identified as having high sanction risks. This action, taken by ABank and Eldik Bank, aims to mitigate sanction risks and enhance financial transparency. Further cooperation with international partners like the EU, US, and UK is planned.

item.title: Suspect in Methamphetamine Distribution Arrested in Astana
item.description: Police in Astana have arrested a 19-year-old woman suspected of storing and distributing narcotics. A search of her rented studio apartment uncovered approximately one kilogram of mephedrone, along with packaging materials. The suspect allegedly acted as a "warehouse," storing drugs for further distribution. An investigation is underway to identify other potential accomplices.

item.title: Flash floods possible in nine regions of Uzbekistan due to expected rainfall
item.description: Flash floods are possible in nine regions of Uzbekistan between November 6-7 and November 9-11 due to expected rainfall. Water accumulation may cause flooding in foothill and mountainous areas. Residents are advised to be cautious.

item.title: Kazakhstan Appoints National Nuclear Center as Radioactive Waste Operator
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Nuclear Center has been designated the operator for radioactive waste management. Established in 1992, the center will oversee the creation and operation of disposal infrastructure, closure of facilities, and management of nuclear heritage sites, addressing decades of accumulated waste from various sources.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Awards Jordanian King Abdullah II the Al-Farabi Order
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev awarded King Abdullah II of Jordan the Al-Farabi Order during the King's visit. Tokayev highlighted the deepening strategic partnership between Kazakhstan and Jordan, noting strong bilateral cooperation and shared priorities.

item.title: Kazpost and Kazakhtelecom Obligated to Pay Monthly Compensation to Disabled Woman
item.description: Kazpost and Kazakhtelecom have been ordered by a court to pay monthly compensation to a woman in the Zhambyl region who became a first-group disabled person after a building roof collapsed on her. The companies must pay 177,000 tenge monthly until she reaches retirement age.

item.title: Jordan's King Abdullah II First Recipient of New Kazakh Order
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev awarded Jordan's King Abdullah II the new Al-Farabi order. Tokayev stated the visit strengthens strategic partnership and bilateral cooperation. King Abdullah II presented Tokayev with Jordan's highest honor, the al-Hussain ibn Ali order, recognizing mutual friendship and respect.

item.title: Kazakhstan National Fund Withdrawals to Exclude Savings Portion, Says National Bank
item.description: Withdrawals from Kazakhstan's National Fund will be covered by the stabilization portfolio, not affecting the savings portion, according to the National Bank. Annual withdrawals of around $8 billion are planned for infrastructure projects. The fund's total assets are $67 billion, with projected long-term returns of $4.2 billion.

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed's Historic Senate Victory Marks New Era for Muslim Americans
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed's election to the US Senate is a landmark achievement for Muslim representation in American politics. The Michigan Democrat's victory over Republican Mike Rogers breaks a generational barrier, bringing a Muslim voice to a powerful institution and marking a significant milestone for the community.

item.title: Eighteen Dead in Suspected Carbon Monoxide Poisonings Across Uzbekistan
item.description: Eighteen people have died in three suspected carbon monoxide poisoning incidents in Uzbekistan between October 25 and November 1. Incidents occurred in the Fergana region, Kokand, and Tashkent, involving family members and children. Investigations point to dangerously modified or illegally imported gas boilers and improper installation as causes.

item.title: Kazakhstan Postpones Tightening of Auto and Mortgage Loan Requirements
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Bank has decided to extend the preferential period for debt-to-income (DTI) ratios on auto and mortgage loans. The DTI for housing loans will be extended for two years until the end of 2029, citing a stable portfolio. For auto loans, the DTI grace period will be extended for one year, as growth has stabilized around 13-14%.

item.title: Verdict Delivered in Shymkent Case Involving Death of Sports Master
item.description: A court in Shymkent has delivered a verdict in the case of the death of 40-year-old sports master Vasily Kolesnikov. Six individuals were charged. The court found defendants guilty of murder, kidnapping, causing serious bodily harm, and hooliganism. Sentences range from 20 to 23 years. One victim, Maksat Koshkenbayev, received 10 million tenge in moral damages.

item.title: Sari Khosor road to be reconstructed, with 54 km from Baljuvon district center to Sari Khosor undergoing work
item.description: The Sari Khosor road is set for reconstruction, with 54 kilometers from the center of Baljuvon district to Sari Khosor already under construction. The project includes building 10 bridges and installing 121 culverts. Over 50 million euros in loans from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development are funding the project.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Prosecutor General Clarifies Laws on Online Extremism
item.description: The Prosecutor General's Office of Kyrgyzstan has issued clarifications on responsibility for storing and distributing extremist materials online. Actions like storing or publishing prohibited content on social media can lead to administrative fines or criminal charges under Kyrgyz law.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Central Bank notes slowing inflation for most goods and services
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank reports a slowdown in price growth for most goods and services within the consumer basket. Deputy Chairman Nodirbek Achilov stated that the trend of prices not falling after rising is not currently observed, citing the currency exchange rate as an example.

item.title: US Open to Mediating Taliban-Pakistan Conflict, Welcomes Pakistan's Anti-Terror Stance
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio indicated Washington's willingness to mediate the conflict between the Taliban and Pakistan if an opportunity arises, while also welcoming Pakistan's efforts against terrorism. Both Pakistan and the Taliban have expressed openness to US mediation, with the Taliban showing greater enthusiasm. Several regional and international powers are also involved in mediation efforts.

item.title: Uzbekistan Achieves Record Cotton Harvest of Over Five Million Tons
item.description: Uzbekistan has harvested over five million tons of raw cotton in 2026, a record since its independence in 1991. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev attributed this success to increased yields and mechanization, despite reduced planting areas. Farmers are expected to profit significantly.
